ei.title: The Role of Order in Effective Teaching
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage:
[1번] Teaching reflects what society itself demands; it necessitates that disorder — of students and teachers alike, of mind, behavior, and environment — yield to its opposite. Effective teaching requires that, failing their own self-imposed order, students experience the imposition of some outer order so that inner order may develop. This means in practice, for instance, that the goals of classes and courses be clearly set, that they be explained and justified, that the manner of achieving them be clear, that the presentation of materials conducive to reaching them be appropriate, and that all activities be directed somehow to their attainment. It means, too, that students take up their own obligation to maintain the conditions under which learning occurs: quiet in their classrooms, respect for and courtesy toward others, civility of language and behavior, and the like. Above all, it implies structured industry — study and activity that are oriented toward a goal and pursued with perseverance and method. That is, good teaching requires that teachers and students subject themselves to external and internal control so that learning can take place.

[2번] When we lecture, scold, yell, or criticize, when we say something positive but in a sarcastic tone, or when we try to make our kids feel guilty, it activates their amygdala, triggering their stress response and putting them into a defensive, rigid, reactive state. Even more basic, when we say no or don't, it releases stress chemicals in our kids' brains (and in ours) that are associated with fear and anger. Functional brain imaging research has shown that even seeing the word no on a screen for less than a second while you're lying in an MRI scanner will cause your brain to suddenly release dozens of stress-producing hormones and neurotransmitters. Conversely, positive words like yes, love, and peace activate systems in the prefrontal cortex that are related to emotional regulation. The problem is that negative words like no and don't have a more powerful effect on kids than positive words. For this reason, the researchers Suniya Luthar and John Gottman say that "bad is stronger than good" when it comes to communicating with children and teens.

[3번] The experiences of learning to ride a bicycle or drive a car illustrate well how the "what" and "how" systems — those involved in object identification and practical action — might interact during development. When we learn to drive a car, we go through a first stage where each required action and sequence of actions — such as looking in the mirror, signaling with the blinker, pressing the clutch prior to shifting into gear, and so forth — are explicitly thought of and double-checked while monitoring our situation in the environment. Once learned and after a few hours of practice, the required actions for driving become second nature, transferable to almost any vehicle and performed without explicit thinking. Information appears to be perceived directly; the affordances of the road, the car, and the traffic implicitly detected. Actually, this sort of automatization of conscious learning can be jeopardized by the return of explicit awareness. If you start to think too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport competitions confirm that self-consciousness is one's worst enemy: tennis, golf, or billiard players commonly report that they lose their "touch" by thinking too much about their moves.

[Gateway] The purpose of class discussions is to encourage you to be an active participant, not a passive recorder. Much of the emphasis in a discussion is on getting students involved in thinking, reacting, and responding. These are important intellectual activities in the learning process, for through them you are supposed to discover and express your opinions. Writing is an invaluable tool for accomplishing these tasks. Unfortunately, too many times, when class discussion begins, pens and pencils go down. Admittedly, it is considerably more difficult to take notes from discussions than from lectures, for, unlike lectures, discussions tend to be disorganized and difficult to follow. Also, students usually don't know how much of what other students are saying is important. And if you are an active participant, it is not easy to take notes and formulate what you want to say. But note taking in discussions is not only manageable, it is also important. Note taking helps to keep you active and alert; it allows you to impose some organization on the discussion; and it can prepare you to speak.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 jeopardized와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ endangered(위험에 빠진): jeopardized와 의미 동일
❌ ① protected(보호된): 반의어
❌ ② improved(개선된): 반대 방향
❌ ④ repeated(반복된): 무관
det.tip: jeopardize = endanger = threaten = put at risk. '위태롭게 하다'의 의미다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① encourage(장려하다): 토론의 목적이 능동 참여 장려라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② active(능동적인): 'an ___ participant' 자리에서 능동적 참여자를 뜻하므로 적절
❌ ③ active → passive: 'not a ___ recorder' 자리는 능동과 대비되는 '수동적' 기록자를 의미하므로 'passive'가 와야 함
✅ ④ thinking(생각하기): 토론에서 강조되는 지적 활동 중 하나로 적절
det.tip: active participant vs passive recorder 는 본문의 핵심 대비 구조이다.

questions.passage: [3번] If you start to __________ (think) too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport competitions confirm that self-consciousness is one's worst enemy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 'start to V' 구조에서 to부정사 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 한다.
det.analysis: 'start to' 뒤에는 to부정사의 동사원형이 와야 하므로 'think'를 그대로 원형으로 쓴다. 'start + to부정사 / 동명사' 모두 가능하지만 빈칸 앞에 'to'가 이미 있으므로 동사원형만 허용된다.
det.tip: to부정사(to + V원형)에서 V는 항상 원형을 유지한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ imposition: 자기 질서가 실패했을 때 학생이 경험해야 하는 것은 '외부 질서의 부과'이다.
❌ ① attainment(달성): 목표에 관한 개념이라 외부 질서의 '경험' 문맥과 다름
❌ ② obligation(의무): 학생이 '지는' 것이며 '경험하는' 것이 아니므로 부적절
❌ ③ method(방법): 'the ___ of some outer order'에 의미상 어울리지 않음
det.tip: experience the imposition of outer order(외부 질서의 부과를 경험하다)는 본문의 핵심 표현이다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① active - invaluable - alert = 원문과 일치
❌ ② passive: 능동적 참여자라는 원문 흐름과 모순
❌ ③ useless: 쓰기가 '매우 귀중한' 도구라는 긍정 서술과 정반대
❌ ④ drowsy: 필기가 학생을 '깨어 있게' 유지한다는 내용과 모순
det.tip: active participant(능동적 참여자), invaluable tool(매우 귀중한 도구), keep you alert(깨어 있게 하다)는 본문의 핵심 표현이다.

questions.passage: [1번] Effective teaching requires that, failing their own self-imposed order, students experience the __________ (impose) of some outer order so that inner order may develop.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 정관사 'the' 뒤에는 명사 형태가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: 정관사 'the' 뒤이자 전치사 'of'의 수식을 받는 자리이므로 동사 'impose'를 명사형 'imposition'으로 바꿔야 한다. 'the imposition of some outer order'는 '어떤 외부 질서의 부과'라는 뜻이다.
det.tip: 동사 impose → 명사 imposition. '-tion' 접미사가 붙어 명사형이 된다.

questions.passage: [Gateway] Much of the emphasis in a discussion is on __________ (get) students involved in thinking, reacting, and responding. These are important intellectual activities in the learning process.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 전치사 on 뒤에는 동명사(-ing) 형태가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: 전치사 'on' 뒤에는 명사 또는 동명사가 와야 하므로 'get'을 동명사 'getting'으로 바꿔야 한다. 'getting students involved'는 '학생들이 참여하도록 하는 것'이라는 뜻이다.
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사(-ing) 구조는 학교 시험 단골 포인트이다.

det.analysis:
✅ ① self-imposed order: 이 질서가 '실패했을 때' 학생이 외부 질서를 경험해야 한다는 맥락이므로 '스스로 부과한 질서'가 정답이다.
❌ ② structured industry(체계적 면학): 본문 후반의 결론 개념이며 '실패'와 어울리지 않음
❌ ③ outer order(외부 질서): 오히려 자기 질서가 실패했을 때 '경험하는 대상'이므로 자리 부적절
❌ ④ civility of language(언행의 예의): 학습 공동체 조건의 하나일 뿐, 'failing'의 대상이 아님
det.tip: failing their own self-imposed order(스스로 부과한 질서가 실패했을 때)는 본문 논리의 출발점이다.

det.analysis:
✅ ① blame(비난하다): criticize와 의미가 가장 가까움
❌ ② praise(칭찬하다): 반의어
❌ ③ reward(보상하다): 반대 개념
❌ ④ forgive(용서하다): 무관
det.tip: criticize의 동의어: blame, condemn, find fault with / 반의어: praise, compliment

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① privilege(특권): 학생이 져야 할 것은 '특권'이 아니라 '의무'이므로 원문과 반대
❌ ② rudeness(무례함): 유지해야 할 것은 '예의'이므로 원문과 정반대
✅ ③ obligation - civility - perseverance = 원문과 일치
❌ ④ laziness(게으름): 체계적 면학은 '인내'로 추구된다는 원문과 모순
det.tip: take up one's obligation(의무를 지다), civility of language(언행의 예의), pursued with perseverance(인내로 추구되는)가 핵심 표현이다.

questions.passage: [Gateway] It is considerably more difficult to take notes from discussions than from lectures, for, unlike lectures, discussions tend to be __________ (disorganize) and difficult to follow.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: be동사 뒤에는 상태를 나타내는 과거분사(수동 형용사) 형태가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: 'tend to be' 뒤에는 형용사/분사 보어가 와야 하며, 토론이 '정돈되지 않은' 상태임을 수동적으로 나타내므로 과거분사 'disorganized'로 바꾼다.
det.tip: be + p.p. 형태의 상태 수동 표현이다. '-ed'로 끝나는 형용사로 기억하자.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② explicitly: 초보 운전자가 각 동작을 '명시적으로' 생각하고 이중 점검한다는 문맥이다. 이후 단락에서 '암묵적으로' 감지되는 숙련 단계와 대조된다.
❌ ① implicitly(암묵적으로): 숙련 단계의 특성이므로 초보 단계의 빈칸에 부적절
❌ ③ directly(직접적으로): 부사지만 '생각하다(thought of)'와 의미가 어울리지 않음
❌ ④ transferable(적용 가능한): 형용사이므로 품사 불일치
det.tip: explicitly thought of(명시적으로 생각되는) vs implicitly detected(암묵적으로 감지되는)는 본문의 핵심 대조.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 release와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ discharge(방출하다): release와 의미 동일. '스트레스 호르몬을 분비하다'라는 본문 의미와 일치
❌ ① store(저장하다): 반대 의미
❌ ② absorb(흡수하다): 반대 의미
❌ ③ hide(숨기다): 무관
det.tip: release hormones/chemicals = discharge/emit hormones. 생물학 지문 단골 표현이다.

questions.passage: [3번] When we learn to drive a car, we go through a first stage where each required action is explicitly thought of. Once __________ (learn) and after a few hours of practice, the required actions become second nature.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 분사구문에서 주어가 생략되고 수동의 의미를 나타낼 때는 과거분사(p.p.)를 사용한다.
det.analysis: 분사구문 'Once __________'는 원래 'Once (it is) learned'에서 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태이다. 동작이 이미 완료된 수동 상태를 나타내므로 과거분사 'learned'로 바꿔야 한다. 영국식 'learnt'도 허용된다.
det.tip: 접속사(Once/When/Although 등) + 과거분사 형태는 분사구문의 축약형이다.

questions.passage: [3번] The experiences of learning to ride a bicycle or drive a car illustrate well how the "what" and "how" systems — those involved in object identification and practical action — might interact during development. When we learn to drive a car, we go through a first stage where each required action and sequence of actions — such as looking in the mirror, signaling with the blinker, pressing the clutch prior to shifting into gear, and so forth — are explicitly thought of and double-checked while monitoring our situation in the environment. Once learned and after a few hours of practice, the required actions for driving become second nature, transferable to almost any vehicle and performed without explicit thinking. Information appears to be (A)[perceived / ignored] directly; the affordances of the road, the car, and the traffic (B)[implicitly / explicitly] detected. Actually, this sort of automatization of (C)[conscious / unconscious] learning can be jeopardized by the return of explicit awareness. If you start to think too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport competitions confirm that self-consciousness is one's worst enemy: tennis, golf, or billiard players commonly report that they lose their "touch" by thinking too much about their moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① ignored: 정보가 '직접 지각된다'는 원문과 정반대
❌ ② explicitly: 숙련 후에는 '암묵적으로' 감지된다는 원문과 모순
✅ ③ perceived - implicitly - conscious = 원문과 일치
❌ ④ unconscious: '의식적 학습(conscious learning)의 자동화'라는 원문과 모순
det.tip: perceived directly(직접 지각되는), implicitly detected(암묵적으로 감지되는), conscious learning(의식적 학습)은 글의 핵심 대조 축이다.

questions.passage: [1번] Above all, it implies structured industry — study and activity that are __________ (orient) toward a goal and pursued with perseverance and method.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: be동사 뒤에는 상태를 나타내는 과거분사(수동 형용사) 형태가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: 'are' 뒤에는 형용사/분사 보어가 와야 하며, 면학 활동이 목표를 향해 '지향된' 상태라는 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 'oriented'로 바꾼다.
det.tip: be oriented toward ~(~을 향해 지향된)는 수동형 관용 표현이다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "using words that mean the opposite of what you really think, especially to mock or show annoyance"

det.analysis:
✅ ② sarcastic: '실제로 생각하는 것과 반대되는 말을 써서 비꼬거나 불쾌함을 드러내는' 태도이다
❌ ① honest(정직한): 정반대 의미
❌ ③ friendly(친근한): 무관
❌ ④ rigid(경직된): 빈정거림과 무관
det.tip: sarcastic tone(빈정거리는 어조)은 겉으로는 긍정적 말이지만 실제로는 부정적 의미를 전달한다.

questions.passage: [Gateway] The purpose of class discussions is to encourage you to be an active participant, not a passive recorder. Much of the emphasis in a discussion is on getting students involved in thinking, reacting, and responding. These are important intellectual activities in the learning process, for through them you are supposed to ①<u>discover</u> and express your opinions. Writing is an invaluable tool for accomplishing these tasks. Unfortunately, too many times, when class discussion begins, pens and pencils go down. Admittedly, it is considerably more difficult to take notes from discussions than from lectures, for, unlike lectures, discussions tend to be disorganized and difficult to follow. Also, students usually don't know how much of what other students are saying is important. And if you are an active participant, it is not easy to take notes and formulate what you want to say. But note taking in discussions is not only manageable, it is also important. Note taking helps to keep you active and ②<u>sleepy</u>; it allows you to ③<u>impose</u> some organization on the discussion; and it can ④<u>prepare</u> you to speak.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① discover(발견하다): 학생들이 토론을 통해 자신의 의견을 '발견하고' 표현한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② sleepy → alert: 필기는 학생을 'active and alert(깨어 있는)' 상태로 유지한다는 원문과 반대
✅ ③ impose(부과하다): 필기가 토론에 어느 정도 체계를 부과한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ prepare(준비시키다): 필기가 말할 준비를 시켜 준다는 원문과 일치
det.tip: keep you active and alert(능동적이고 깨어 있게 유지하다)는 필기의 효용을 나타내는 핵심 구문이다.

questions.passage: [1번] Teaching reflects what society itself demands; it necessitates that (A)[disorder / harmony] — of students and teachers alike, of mind, behavior, and environment — yield to its opposite. Effective teaching requires that, failing their own self-imposed order, students experience the imposition of some (B)[outer / (C)[inner / outer]] order so that inner order may develop. This means in practice, for instance, that the goals of classes and courses be clearly set, that they be explained and justified, that the manner of achieving them be clear, that the presentation of materials conducive to reaching them be appropriate, and that all activities be directed somehow to their attainment. It means, too, that students take up their own obligation to maintain the conditions under which learning occurs: quiet in their classrooms, respect for and courtesy toward others, civility of language and behavior, and the like. Above all, it implies structured industry — study and activity that are oriented toward a goal and pursued with perseverance and method. That is, good teaching requires that teachers and students subject themselves to external and internal control so that learning can take place.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① disorder - outer - inner = 원문과 일치
❌ ② harmony: 가르침이 극복해야 할 대상을 '조화'라 하면 원문 흐름과 정반대
❌ ③ inner(내부의): 학생이 먼저 경험하는 것은 '외부의(outer) 질서'라는 원문과 모순
❌ ④ outer(외부의): 궁극적으로 발달하는 것은 '내적(inner) 질서'라는 원문과 반대
det.tip: outer order(외부 질서)를 경험해야 inner order(내적 질서)가 발달한다는 본문의 핵심 대비 구조를 기억하자.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 disorganized와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① orderly(질서 있는, 정돈된): disorganized의 반의어
❌ ② messy(어질러진): 유의어
❌ ③ random(무작위의): 유의어에 가까움
❌ ④ unclear(불분명한): 관련은 있으나 반의어는 아님
det.tip: disorganized = messy, chaotic ↔ orderly, organized, structured
